text: The 2018 Web of Microbes snapshot uses action meanings that differ between control and organism entries.
quote: The WoM database encodes metabolite observations with a 4-action system that differs between control and organism entries:
heading: 1. WoM Action Encoding Uses Four Distinct Semantics, Not Three

text: Action counts are control D 742 and N 1,023; organism I 1,338, E 1,155, and N 7,509. N has different control and organism meanings.
quote:
| Control ("The Environment") | D | Detected in starting medium | 742 |
| Control ("The Environment") | N | Not detected | 1,023 |
| Organisms | I | Increased (present in medium, level went up) | 1,338 |
| Organisms | E | Emerged (NOT in medium, now detected = de novo production) | 1,155 |
| Organisms | N | No significant change | 7,509 |
heading: 1. WoM Action Encoding Uses Four Distinct Semantics, Not Three

text: E means a metabolite emerged after being absent from starting medium; I means an existing metabolite increased. The report states zero E/I overlap across 10,744 observations, although the displayed action counts have a different total.
quote: **'E' and 'I' are mutually exclusive** (zero overlap across all 10,744 observations). 'E' encodes genuine de novo metabolite synthesis — the organism produced a metabolite that was absent from the starting medium. This distinction is biologically meaningful: 'I' represents amplification of existing metabolites, while 'E' represents novel biosynthetic output.
heading: 1. WoM Action Encoding Uses Four Distinct Semantics, Not Three

text: The 2018 export has no organism consumption/decrease action; all 742 D records are controls. Consumption data in a newer version is possible but unverified.
quote: **There is no "Decreased" (consumption) action for any organism** in this 2018 snapshot. All 742 'D' observations belong exclusively to the control. The original Kosina et al. (2018) paper describes "decrease" as a valid action, so consumption data may exist in the newer GNPS2 version.
heading: 1. WoM Action Encoding Uses Four Distinct Semantics, Not Three

heading: 4. 26.8% of WoM Metabolites Have Definitive ModelSEED Links (68.5% with Ambiguous Formula Matches)

text: Exact names provide definitive ModelSEED links for 69 of 257 identified compounds. Formula-only links for 107 compounds are ambiguous, averaging 8.4 ModelSEED molecules per formula, and require manual curation.
quote: Of 257 identified (non-unknown) WoM compounds, **69 (26.8%) have definitive ModelSEED links** by exact name match. An additional 107 match by molecular formula alone, but formula matches are inherently ambiguous — each WoM formula maps to an average of 8.4 ModelSEED molecules (e.g., C5H11NO2 matches valine, norvaline, betaine, 5-aminopentanoate, and others). Formula matches provide candidate sets for manual curation, not definitive identifications.
heading: 4. 26.8% of WoM Metabolites Have Definitive ModelSEED Links (68.5% with Ambiguous Formula Matches)

text: Of 589 tracked metabolites, 332 (56.4%) are unidentified. The statement that 408 of 257 identified metabolites changed is internally impossible, although 408 is also given as 69.3% of all 589. Named active compounds include amino acids and nucleotides.
quote: 589 metabolites are tracked, of which 332 (56.4%) are unidentified ("Unk_" prefix). Of the 257 identified metabolites, 408 (69.3% of all 589) show at least one change across the database. The most metabolically active compounds are amino acids (glutamine, proline, phenylalanine) and nucleotides (adenine, adenosine, guanine).
heading: Database Scale

text: Simple metabolite-name matching to GapMind pathways failed because pathway identifiers lack metabolite names; a substrate/product lookup is needed.
quote: **WoM ↔ GapMind**: Blocked by naming convention mismatch. GapMind pathway names (internal IDs) don't contain simple metabolite names. A proper lookup table mapping GapMind pathways to substrate/product metabolites is needed.
heading: Cross-Collection Link Quality

text: Pangenome linkage is genus-level only; strain-to-genome mapping needed for species-level linkage was not attempted.
quote: **WoM ↔ Pangenome**: Available at genus level for all WoM organisms. Species-level matching requires strain-to-genome mapping (not attempted in this project).
heading: Cross-Collection Link Quality

text: The report judges its cross-collection integration hypothesis partially, not fully, supported.
quote: **H1 is partially supported.** Cross-collection links are real and actionable:
heading: Hypothesis Outcome

text: Absent consumption observations prevent testing whether consumed metabolites predict gene essentiality. The data cover 37 organism entries and five projects from one laboratory.
quote: However, the **absence of consumption data** is a fundamental limitation. The 2018 WoM snapshot records only what organisms produce, not what they consume. This prevents testing the most interesting question — whether consumed metabolites predict gene essentiality. The data is also small (37 organisms, 5 projects) and from a single laboratory.
heading: Hypothesis Outcome

text: The original WoM publication describes decrease as a valid schema action, but this export lacks it.
quote: **Kosina et al. (2018)** introduced WoM with the same data we analyzed. Their paper describes "decrease" as a valid action, confirming that consumption data is part of the WoM schema but absent from this specific export.
heading: Literature Context

text: The Literature Context section reports NLDM-supported growth for 108/110 diverse soil bacteria with metabolites trackable by LC-MS/MS. There, consumption data and GNPS2 availability are qualified as likely or possible; Future Directions makes a stronger consumption-and-production assertion.
quote: **de Raad et al. (2022)** developed the Northen Lab Defined Medium (NLDM) supporting growth of 108/110 phylogenetically diverse soil bacteria, with all metabolites trackable via LC-MS/MS. This represents a major expansion of the exometabolomics approach and likely contains consumption data. The NLDM dataset may be available in the current GNPS2 version of WoM.
heading: Literature Context

text: Only 20 of 37 organism entries are experimental; the report says the set is too small for between-group statistical analysis.
quote: - **Small organism set**: 37 organisms (20 experimental) is too few for statistical analyses across organism groups.
heading: Limitations

text: The archived 2018 snapshot may not represent current WoM; richer GNPS2 or Northen lab datasets are suggested but were not analyzed.
quote: - **2018 frozen snapshot**: The Wayback Machine archive may not reflect the current state of WoM. The GNPS2-hosted version or the Northen lab's internal datasets (including the NLDM 110-organism panel from de Raad et al. 2022) would be substantially richer.
heading: Limitations

text: Future Directions asserts that the NLDM study tested 110 soil bacteria with full consumption and production tracking, more strongly than Literature Context's statement that consumption data are likely. It conditionally projects that ingesting this dataset would resolve the snapshot's no-consumption limitation and increase organism count 3–5×; neither ingestion nor that increase occurred in this project.
quote: 1. **Obtain the current WoM dataset from GNPS2 or the Northen lab**: The de Raad et al. (2022) NLDM study tested 110 soil bacteria with full consumption and production tracking. This dataset, if ingested, would resolve the no-consumption limitation and increase the organism count 3–5×.
heading: Future Directions

text: Testing whether produced metabolites predict gene fitness in the two matched Pseudomonas strains remains future work, not a demonstrated result.
quote: 3. **Gene fitness ↔ metabolite production analysis**: For pseudo3_N2E3 and pseudo13_GW456_L13, identify which genes are fitness-important on carbon sources that the same organism produces. This tests whether metabolic output predicts gene essentiality.
heading: Future Directions

text: The proposed E/(E+I)-versus-pangenome-openness association remains untested; this explicit ratio also highlights the unclear denominator of the reported novelty percentages.
quote: 4. **Metabolic novelty rate ↔ pangenome openness**: Test whether organisms with higher E/(E+I) ratios (more de novo production) have more open pangenomes or more accessory genes.
